title: Choosing how much a callout magnifies before you draw it
goal: You can now choose whether the next zoom callout is a box or a circle before you draw it, but not how much it magnifies: that number only exists on a callout you have already drawn, and it lives in the right hand panel, so with the panel hidden there is no way to it at all. The tool should carry its own starting magnification, next to its shape, and remember what you last chose.
notes: Follow-up from queue/audits/2026-09-05-tool-settings.json rough 3. The capsule is Sources/Photonz/ToolSettingsCapsule.swift and its contents are decided by ToolSettingsBar.settings(for:availability:) in PhotonzCore; add a .calloutMagnification case there with a test. The tool-level shape precedent is EditorState.calloutToolShape (EditorState+MeasurePanel.swift:243) and ZoomCalloutBuilder.defaultMagnification / magnificationRange are the numbers. The picked-layer control is CalloutInspector and must not move.
acceptance: The Zoom Callout tool carries a starting magnification next to its Shape, reachable with the right hand panel hidden
A callout drawn after changing it comes out at that magnification
The tool remembers the last magnification chosen, across windows and across launches
A callout already on the canvas is still changed in its own section of the panel, and that section is unchanged

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) The existing CalloutStyles doc says magnification must not be remembered because 'it comes out of the drag'. Half true: a corner pull sets it, but the DRAG never does — every new callout is hardcoded 2x. So the tool has a starting magnification whether we admit it or not; the real hazard the comment names is the tool quietly absorbing whatever the last corner pull left behind. Design rule taken from it: the tool's number changes ONLY when you move the tool's own control, never when a placed callout is resized. (2) Value beyond 'draw then resize': resizing a placed callout grows it around its own centre, so it can end up over another callout or off the picture; drawing at the right magnification lets placement pick a clear spot first time. (3) Shortest version: one short slider plus a readout, exactly the wand tolerance control already in the capsule, not a stepper or a numeric field. (4) Order: Shape stays first and Magnification is added after it, in both the capsule and the panel's Zoom Callout Tool section, so a setting that is already there does not get shoved. (5) Width check: Shape (~164pt) + 18 + Magnification (~222pt) is about 404pt against the 448pt narrowest picture the app allows, so it still does not wrap.

Built. Core: CalloutStyles gains a clamped magnification (ZoomCalloutBuilder.clampedMagnification), ToolSetting gains .calloutMagnification and the zoom callout's capsule list is now [shape, magnification] behind its own Availability flag. App: next-callout-magnification in the Next catalog (on by default), EditorState.calloutToolMagnification persisted to the calloutStyles blob, addZoomCallout passes it, a short slider plus readout in the capsule and a Magnification row in the panel's Zoom Callout Tool section. Verified live in the probe with Scripts/playtest/callout-magnification-walk.json: tool at 2x draws 2.0x; pulling the PICKED callout to 4.0x leaves the tool on 2.0x (the tool never absorbs a resize); tool armed to 4x draws 4.0x and the second callout is placed clear of the first at that size; back to 2x draws 2.0x again. Persistence proved both ways because the walk harness restores settings at teardown: the choice is written into the app's settings while it runs, and a launch seeded with 4.0x comes up on 4.0x. Scripts/test.sh green, 3756 tests. Screen Recording was granted, so the audit carries real window captures.

Adversarial review of the built thing. Kept: the capsule is now ~440pt wide for this tool against Measure's 340pt, so it covers more of the bottom band - flagged for the user rather than shrunk, since trimming the slider buys ~12pt and costs precision. Kept: neither slider snaps, so 3.0x takes a careful hand; matching the drawn callout's existing slider beat inventing a second behaviour. Found and left as a note: a 360x240pt region at 4x now fills a 1440x960 canvas in one drag, which is placed on canvas and undoable but unannounced. Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-06-callout-magnification.json.

The Zoom Callout tool carries a Magnification slider beside its Shape, in the capsule above the tool bar (so it is there with the panel hidden) and in the panel's Zoom Callout Tool section, both one value. New callouts come out at it, it is remembered across launches, and a placed callout's own slider is unchanged and never re-arms the tool. Verified live in the probe with Scripts/playtest/callout-magnification-walk.json; Scripts/test.sh green (3756). Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-06-callout-magnification.json. Commit fc4ade1.
